messages:
sara: Quick sync — need final PRD acceptance criteria and QA checklist for the authz launch (org/projects + scoped tokens). Main asks: customer rollouts want predictable scoping, token rotation, and clear fallback behavior. @aj can you sketch the final acceptance bullets?

aj: Yep. Drafting now. High level AC I'm proposing: 1) API keys and scoped tokens must reject cross-org access by default. 2) Project-level RBAC policies evaluate and block unauthorized ops with 403 + structured error code. 3) Token TTLs configurable with enforced max cap by org policy. 4) Token rotation endpoint returns new token and invalidates old one atomically. 5) Audit log entries for all token creations/deletes include actor, org_id, project_id, and token_id.

mike: +1 on those. Edge cases we need explicit behavior for: service-to-service delegation (token exchange), long-lived service tokens vs short-lived scoped tokens, and fallback when KMS is temporarily unavailable. Also need clear error codes for stale cache vs authz deny.

nora: For rollout strategy: default behavior for existing customers should be no-op (legacy API keys continue to work) unless they opt-in to strict project scoping. New accounts get stricter defaults. We also need a migration plan for orgs that have 3rd-party integrations relying on global keys.

sara: Good — migration + rollback criteria should be part of launch gating. Proposed gating: (a) end-to-end e2e tests passing for cross-org block, (b) perf < 10ms authz eval P50 at peak QPS in staging, (c) no unhandled 500s from KMS in 72h soak, (d) docs + SDK snippets published.

aj: Adding acceptance test matrix snippets here:
```
- create org A, project p1, key scoped to org A:p1
- attempt read from org B -> expect 403 AUTHZ_CROSS_ORG
- rotate token -> old token returns 401 TOKEN_REVOKED
- delegate using token-exchange -> if target scope narrower succeed else 403
- simulate KMS latency -> policy: degrade to deny (fail-closed) with telemetry flag
```

mike: Please ensure tests assert structured error body shape: { "code": "AUTHZ_CROSS_ORG", "message": "...", "meta": {"org_id":"...","resource":"..."} }. That helps operators and customers map failures. Also include replay prevention for token reuse after rotation.

nora: Ops notes: KMS integration must surface metrics: key_fetch_latency, key_fetch_error_rate, rotation_success_rate. For private deployments, note that HSM/KMS mapping may be customer-provided — include explicit fallback policy docs.

sara: Edge cases list (short bullets) to include in PRD: 1) orphaned projects after org transfer, 2) API key used across multiple regions with eventual consistency, 3) simultaneous rotation requests for same token, 4) expired cached policies during rollout.

aj: Implementation notes: we'll introduce a token metadata header with fields: org_id, project_id, issued_at, expires_at, parent_token_id (optional). Example header:```
Authorization: Bearer scoped_org:123_proj:456_issued:1670000000_exp:1670003600_sig:...
```

mike: Security requirements: require KMS-backed signing for scoped tokens in production; deterministic token_id format that doesn't leak PII; rate limit token-create endpoints to avoid abuse. Also add a CVE response plan for key compromise (revoke-all for affected org).

sara: UX & docs: need SDK helper: `createScopedToken({org,project,ttl})` + example for rotating on failure (401 -> rotate -> retry). Also include migration script for bulk-scoping existing keys.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: staging-authz-tests: 0 failed, staging-kms-soak: 1h running, docs-published: false

sara: Action items: @aj produce PRD w/ AC + test matrix by EOD tomorrow; @mike write security appendix (KMS, rotation, incident plan); @nora draft rollout runbook + metrics dashboard requirements. I'll schedule a quick sync after drafts. :thumbsup:

aj: noted, will push an initial PRD link here when ready. :eyes:

mike: I'll drop a short threat model and incident playbook section into the PRD.

nora: I'll add metrics and runbook skeleton to the ops doc, and a migration checklist for partner integrations.

sara: Perfect. If no blockers, we aim for soft-launch to a pilot account group in 3 weeks. We'll use telemetry and canary routing to limit blast radius.

sara: quick final question — decision needed on default token lifetime cap. My suggestion: orgs may configure up to 30d for service tokens but scoped ephemeral tokens default to 1h. Thoughts?

mike: Default 1h ephemeral is good. Allow up to 30d for service tokens but require org admin approval + audit log and a warning in the UI.

aj: fine with that. We'll enforce server-side max TTL with config for Dedicated/Private deployments.

sara: Great — I'll record that in PRD. Everyone please drop any missing edge cases in this thread. Thanks! :rocket:
